task_prompt: Inside a frame, draw 1 yellow center circle and arrange 8 elliptical petals around it in a radial pattern (e.g., one petal on each compass direction plus diagonals). Each petal is a different color.

text: I'll help you create a flower design with a yellow center circle and 8 colorful elliptical petals arranged radially. Let me start by taking a screenshot to see the current state of the application.

I can see this is a design application (appears to be Figma or similar). I need to:
1. First draw a frame
2. Then draw a yellow center circle
3. Add 8 elliptical petals in different colors arranged radially

Let me start by drawing a frame. I'll press 'R' to draw a rectangle as mentioned in the layers panel hint, but I'll actually need to use the frame tool. Let me click on the frame tool in the toolbar.
Great! I clicked on the frame tool and a menu opened showing various frame presets. I'll select a desktop frame to have a good working area. Let me click on "Desktop".
Good, the Desktop section is now expanded. I'll click on "Desktop" (1440×1024) to create a frame.

Perfect! A Desktop frame has been created. I can see it in the layers panel on the left and the properties on the right. Now I need to draw elements on the canvas. Let me click in the center of the canvas to place the frame or I can try to draw on the canvas directly. Let me first click on the canvas area to see the frame better.

I see the canvas is now showing. The frame is created but I need to see it better. Let me click on the Desktop frame in the layers panel to make sure it's selected, then I'll zoom in or adjust the view to see it better.
Good, the Desktop frame is selected. Now I need to zoom to fit the frame in view. Let me use the keyboard shortcut Shift+1 to zoom to fit.

The view hasn't changed much. Let me try to click on the canvas area to see the frame or try to create a smaller custom frame. Actually, let me first delete this frame and create a simpler one that will be easier to work with. Let me press Delete to remove it.
Good! The frame has been deleted. Now let me create a custom frame. I'll press 'F' to use the frame tool and draw a custom-sized frame.

Perfect! The frame tool is now active and showing preset options. I can see the frame icon is highlighted in the toolbar at the bottom. Instead of using a preset, let me just draw a custom frame on the canvas. I'll click and drag on the canvas to create a frame.

Excellent! I've created a frame (400×400 pixels) shown in the canvas. I can see "Frame 1" in the layers panel on the left and the frame properties on the right. Now I need to draw the flower inside this frame:

1. First, I'll draw the yellow center circle
2. Then I'll add 8 elliptical petals in different colors arranged radially

Let me start by drawing the center circle. I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The ellipse tool is now active (I can see it's highlighted in the toolbar). Now I'll draw a circle in the center of the frame. To make it a perfect circle, I'll hold Shift while dragging. Let me draw it in the center of the frame.

Great! I've created a perfect circle (80×80 pixels) in the center of the frame. Now I need to change its color to yellow. I can see the FILL section on the right panel showing "D9D9D9" (gray). Let me click on the fill color to change it to yellow.
Perfect! A color picker has opened. I can see the color spectrum at the bottom. I need to select yellow. Let me click on the yellow area of the color spectrum bar at the bottom.
Good! The color picker is now showing yellow tones. Now I need to select a bright yellow from the color square. I'll click in the top-right area to get a bright, vivid yellow.

Excellent! The center circle is now a bright yellow color (EDC218). I can see it's displayed in the canvas. Now I need to close the color picker and start creating the petals. Let me press Escape to close the color picker.

Perfect! The color picker is closed and I can see the yellow center circle in the frame. Now I need to create 8 elliptical petals arranged radially around it. The petals should be positioned at:
- North (top)
- Northeast 
- East (right)
- Southeast
- South (bottom)
- Southwest
- West (left)
- Northwest

Let me start by drawing an ellipse for the first petal. I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Good! The ellipse tool is active (I can see it highlighted in the toolbar). Now I'll draw the first petal at the top (north position). I'll draw a vertical ellipse that extends upward from the center circle.

Perfect! I've created the first petal - a gray ellipse (40×60 pixels) positioned at the top. I can see it's currently selected and showing in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to change its color to something other than yellow. Let me make this first petal red. I'll click on the fill color.
Great! The color picker has opened. I can see the spectrum bar at the bottom showing various colors. I'll select red for this first petal. Let me click on the red area of the spectrum.
Good! The color picker is now showing red/orange tones. Now I need to select a bright red from the color square. I'll click in the top-right area to get a vibrant red.

Perfect! The first petal is now red (ED2F18) and positioned at the top (north). I can see it displayed above the yellow center circle. Now let me close the color picker and create the next petal. I'll press Escape.

Excellent! The color picker is closed. I can see the red petal at the top and the yellow center circle. Now I need to create 7 more petals in different colors. Let me continue with the next petal at the northeast position (45 degrees). I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Good! The ellipse tool is active (I can see it's highlighted in the toolbar). Now I'll draw the second petal at the northeast position - diagonally up and to the right from the center. To create a petal that's rotated at 45 degrees, I'll draw an ellipse in that direction.

Good! I've created another ellipse (42×42 pixels), but it's appearing as a circle rather than an elongated petal. I need to rotate it to align with the diagonal direction. However, I think it would be better to first resize it to make it more petal-like (elliptical and longer), and then rotate it to 45 degrees. Let me first change the dimensions. I can see the LAYOUT section shows W: 42 and H: 42. Let me change the height to make it more elliptical. I'll click on the height field.
The height field is now selected (showing 42). Let me change it to 60 to make it more elliptical.
Good! The height field now shows 60. Let me press Enter to apply this change.

Perfect! The ellipse is now taller (42×60) and more petal-like. Now I need to rotate it to 45 degrees so it aligns with the northeast diagonal direction. I can see the rotation field (∠) showing 0 in the POSITION section. Let me click on the rotation field to change it to 45 degrees.
Good! The rotation field is now selected (showing 0). Let me type 45 to rotate the petal to the northeast diagonal.
Perfect! The rotation field now shows 45. Let me press Enter to apply the rotation.

Excellent! The ellipse has been rotated 45 degrees and is now positioned diagonally. I can see it's rotated and currently shows in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to change its color. Let me click on the fill color to make this petal a different color - let's make it orange.
Perfect! The color picker has opened. I can see the spectrum at the bottom. I'll select orange for this petal. Let me click on the orange area of the spectrum bar.

Great! The color picker is now showing orange tones. I can see the spectrum bar has an indicator on orange. Now I need to select a bright orange from the color square. I'll click in the top-right area to get a vibrant orange.

Perfect! The second petal is now a bright orange color (ED8818) and positioned in the northeast diagonal (45 degrees). I can see it in the canvas. Now let me close the color picker and continue with the remaining 6 petals. I'll press Escape.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can now see the flower taking shape with:
- Yellow center circle
- Red petal at the top (north)
- Orange petal at the northeast diagonal

Now I need to create the remaining 6 petals:
- East (right)
- Southeast
- South (bottom)
- Southwest
- West (left)
- Northwest

Let me continue by creating the third petal on the right (east position). I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The ellipse tool is active (highlighted in the toolbar at the bottom). Now I'll draw the third petal on the right (east position). This should be a horizontal ellipse extending to the right from the center circle.

Perfect! I've created an ellipse (60×40 pixels) positioned to the right. I can see it's currently selected and showing the dimensions "60 × 40" in the canvas. The ellipse is in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to rotate it 90 degrees so it's oriented horizontally (pointing outward from the center). Let me click on the rotation field to change it to 90 degrees.
I can see the rotation field shows 0 and is selected. Let me type 90 to rotate the ellipse horizontally.
Perfect! The rotation field now shows 90. Let me press Enter to apply the rotation.

Excellent! The ellipse has been rotated 90 degrees and is now oriented horizontally, extending to the right from the center. I can see it positioned on the right side (east position). It's currently in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to change its color. Let me click on the fill color to make it a different color - let's make it pink/magenta.
Perfect! The color picker has opened and I can see the color spectrum at the bottom. I'll select a pink/magenta color for this third petal. Let me click on the magenta/pink area of the spectrum.

Great! The color picker is now showing magenta/pink tones. I can see the spectrum indicator is on the pink/magenta area. Now I'll click in the top-right area of the color square to get a bright, vivid magenta/pink color.

Perfect! The third petal is now a bright magenta/pink color (ED18C2) and positioned on the right (east position). I can see it in the canvas extending horizontally to the right. Now let me close the color picker and continue with the remaining 5 petals. I'll press Escape.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can now see the flower developing beautifully with:
- Yellow center circle
- Red petal at the top (north)
- Orange petal at the northeast diagonal
- Magenta/pink petal at the right (east)

Now I need to create the remaining 5 petals:
- Southeast (135 degrees)
- South (180 degrees)
- Southwest (225 degrees)
- West (270 degrees)
- Northwest (315 degrees)

Let me continue by creating the fourth petal at the southeast position (135 degrees). I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The ellipse tool is now active (I can see it's highlighted in the toolbar at the bottom). Now I'll draw the fourth petal at the southeast diagonal position (down and to the right from the center). I'll draw an ellipse in that area.

Perfect! I've created another ellipse (42×42 pixels) positioned in the southeast area. I can see it's currently selected and displayed as a circle. Now I need to:
1. Resize it to make it more elliptical (change height to 60)
2. Rotate it to 135 degrees to align with the southeast diagonal

Let me first change the height. I'll click on the height field in the LAYOUT section.
Good! The height field is now selected (showing 42 in blue). Let me type 60 to make it more elliptical.
Perfect! The height field now shows 60. Let me press Enter to apply this change.

Excellent! The ellipse is now taller (42×60) as shown by the dimension label "42 × 60" in the canvas. Now I need to rotate it to 135 degrees so it aligns with the southeast diagonal direction. Let me click on the rotation field to change it.
Good! The rotation field is now selected (showing 0 highlighted in blue). Let me type 135 to rotate the petal to the southeast diagonal.
Perfect! The rotation field now shows 135. Let me press Enter to apply the rotation.

Excellent! The ellipse has been rotated 135 degrees and is now positioned diagonally in the southeast direction. I can see it's rotated correctly, extending down and to the right from the center. The ellipse is currently in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to change its color. Let me click on the fill color to make it a different color - let's make it purple/violet.

Perfect! The color picker has opened and I can see the full color spectrum bar at the bottom. I'll select a purple/violet color for this fourth petal. Let me click on the blue-purple area of the spectrum.

Great! The color picker is now showing purple/violet tones. I can see the color square showing purple/violet gradients and the spectrum indicator is on the purple area. Now I'll click in the top-right area of the color square to get a bright, vivid purple.

Perfect! The fourth petal is now a bright purple/violet color (6818ED) and positioned at the southeast diagonal (135 degrees). I can see it displayed in the canvas at the lower-right diagonal. Now let me close the color picker and continue with the remaining 4 petals. I'll press Escape.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can now see the flower developing beautifully with 5 elements so far:
- Yellow center circle
- Red petal at the top (north)
- Orange petal at the northeast diagonal
- Magenta/pink petal at the right (east)
- Purple/violet petal at the southeast diagonal

Now I need to create the remaining 4 petals:
- South (bottom) - 180 degrees
- Southwest - 225 degrees
- West (left) - 270 degrees
- Northwest - 315 degrees

Let me continue by creating the fifth petal at the bottom (south position). I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The ellipse tool is now active (I can see it's highlighted in the toolbar at the bottom). Now I'll draw the fifth petal at the bottom (south position). This should be a vertical ellipse extending downward from the center circle.

Perfect! I've created an ellipse (40×60 pixels) positioned at the bottom. I can see it's currently selected with the dimension label "40 × 60" in the canvas. The ellipse is in gray (D9D9D9). For the south petal, I need to rotate it 180 degrees to point downward. Let me click on the rotation field to change it.
Good! The rotation field shows 0 and is selected. Let me type 180 to rotate the ellipse to point downward (south direction).
Perfect! The rotation field now shows 180. Let me press Enter to apply the rotation.

Excellent! The ellipse has been rotated 180 degrees and is now pointing downward (south position). I can see it's correctly positioned at the bottom, extending downward from the center. The ellipse is currently in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to change its color. Let me click on the fill color to make it a different color - let's make it blue.
Perfect! The color picker has opened and I can see the full color spectrum bar at the bottom. I'll select a blue color for this fifth petal. Let me click on the blue area of the spectrum.

Great! The color picker is now showing blue tones. I can see the color square displaying blue gradients and the spectrum indicator is on the blue area. Now I'll click in the top-right area of the color square to get a bright, vivid blue.

Perfect! The fifth petal is now a bright cyan/blue color (18B3ED) and positioned at the bottom (south position, 180 degrees). I can see it displayed in the canvas extending downward from the center. Now let me close the color picker and continue with the remaining 3 petals. I'll press Escape.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can now see the flower developing beautifully with 6 elements so far:
- Yellow center circle
- Red petal at the top (north)
- Orange petal at the northeast diagonal
- Magenta/pink petal at the right (east)
- Purple/violet petal at the southeast diagonal
- Cyan/blue petal at the bottom (south)

Now I need to create the remaining 3 petals:
- Southwest - 225 degrees
- West (left) - 270 degrees
- Northwest - 315 degrees

Let me continue by creating the sixth petal at the southwest position (225 degrees). I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The ellipse tool is now active (I can see it's highlighted with a bright blue color in the toolbar at the bottom). Now I'll draw the sixth petal at the southwest diagonal position (down and to the left from the center). I'll draw an ellipse in that area.

Perfect! I've created another ellipse (42×42 pixels) positioned in the southwest area. I can see it's currently selected with selection handles visible and the dimension label "42 × 42" in the canvas. The LAYOUT section shows W: 42 and H: 42. Now I need to:
1. Resize it to make it more elliptical (change height to 60)
2. Rotate it to 225 degrees to align with the southwest diagonal

Let me first change the height. I'll click on the height field.
Good! The height field is now selected (showing 42 highlighted in blue). Let me type 60 to make it more elliptical.
Perfect! The height field now shows 60. Let me press Enter to apply this change.

Excellent! The ellipse is now taller (42×60) as shown by the dimension label "42 × 60" in the canvas. Now I need to rotate it to 225 degrees so it aligns with the southwest diagonal direction. Let me click on the rotation field to change it.
Good! The rotation field is now selected (showing 0 highlighted). Let me type 225 to rotate the petal to the southwest diagonal.
Perfect! The rotation field now shows 225. Let me press Enter to apply the rotation.

Excellent! The ellipse has been rotated 225 degrees and is now positioned diagonally in the southwest direction. I can see it's rotated correctly, extending down and to the left from the center. The ellipse is currently in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to change its color. Let me click on the fill color to make it a different color - let's make it green.
Perfect! The color picker has opened and I can see the full color spectrum bar at the bottom. I'll select a green color for this sixth petal. Let me click on the green area of the spectrum.

Great! The color picker is now showing green tones. I can see the color square displaying green gradients and the spectrum indicator is on the green area. Now I'll click in the top-right area of the color square to get a bright, vivid green.

Perfect! The sixth petal is now a bright green color (2DED18) and positioned at the southwest diagonal (225 degrees). I can see it displayed in the canvas at the lower-left diagonal. Now let me close the color picker and continue with the remaining 2 petals. I'll press Escape.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can now see the flower developing beautifully with 7 elements so far:
- Yellow center circle
- Red petal at the top (north)
- Orange petal at the northeast diagonal
- Magenta/pink petal at the right (east)
- Purple/violet petal at the southeast diagonal
- Cyan/blue petal at the bottom (south)
- Green petal at the southwest diagonal

Now I need to create the remaining 2 petals:
- West (left) - 270 degrees
- Northwest - 315 degrees

Let me continue by creating the seventh petal at the left (west position). I'll press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The ellipse tool is now active (I can see it's highlighted in bright blue in the toolbar at the bottom). Now I'll draw the seventh petal at the left (west position). This should be a horizontal ellipse extending to the left from the center circle.

Perfect! I've created an ellipse (60×40 pixels) positioned to the left. I can see it's currently selected with the dimension label "60 × 40" in the canvas and the LAYOUT section shows W: 60 and H: 40. The ellipse is in gray (D9D9D9). For the west petal, I need to rotate it 270 degrees so it points to the left. Let me click on the rotation field to change it.
I can see the screen, but I need to find the rotation field. Let me scroll up in the right panel to see the rotation field in the POSITION section.

I can see the POSITION section at the top, but I need to see if there's a rotation field visible. I can see there's a small rotation icon (∠) with a field showing "0" in the POSITION section. Let me click on that field to enter the rotation value.
I can see the rotation field shows 0 in the POSITION section. It appears to be selected now. Let me type 270 to rotate the petal to point to the left (west direction).
Perfect! The rotation field now shows 270 in the POSITION section. Let me press Enter to apply the rotation.

Excellent! The ellipse has been rotated 270 degrees and is now pointing to the left (west position). I can see it's positioned correctly on the left side of the flower, extending horizontally to the left from the center. The ellipse is currently in gray (D9D9D9). Now I need to change its color. Let me scroll down a bit to see the fill color field and change it to a different color. Let me make this one light blue/cyan or turquoise.

Perfect! Now I can see the FILL section showing "D9D9D9" (gray). Let me click on the fill color square to change the color to something different. Let me make this seventh petal a different color - I'll try an indigo or dark blue color.

Perfect! The color picker has opened and I can see the full color spectrum bar at the bottom with all the colors. I need to select a different color for this seventh petal. Since I've already used many colors, let me choose a teal/turquoise color. Let me click on the cyan-green area of the spectrum.

Great! The color picker is now showing teal/cyan-green tones. I can see the color square displaying teal/turquoise gradients and the spectrum indicator is on that area. Now I'll click in the top-right area of the color square to get a bright, vivid teal/turquoise.

Perfect! The seventh petal is now a bright teal/turquoise color (18EB94) and positioned at the left (west position, 270 degrees). I can see it displayed in the canvas on the left side of the flower, colored in a beautiful cyan-green/teal. Now let me close the color picker and create the final eighth petal. I'll press Escape.

Excellent! The color picker is closed and I can now see the flower almost complete with 8 elements:
- Yellow center circle
- Red petal at the top (north)
- Orange petal at the northeast diagonal
- Magenta/pink petal at the right (east)
- Purple/violet petal at the southeast diagonal
- Cyan/blue petal at the bottom (south)
- Green petal at the southwest diagonal
- Teal/turquoise petal at the left (west)

Now I need to create the final eighth petal at the northwest position (315 degrees). Let me press 'O' to use the ellipse tool.

Perfect! The ellipse tool is now active (I can see it's highlighted in bright blue in the toolbar at the bottom). Now I'll draw the final eighth petal at the northwest diagonal position (up and to the left from the center). I'll draw an ellipse in that area.

Perfect! I've created another ellipse (42×42 pixels) positioned in the northwest area. I can see it's currently selected with selection handles visible and the dimension label "42 × 42" in the canvas. The LAYOUT section shows W: 42 and H: 42. Now I need to:
1. Resize it to make it more elliptical (change height to 60)
2. Rotate it to 315 degrees to align with the northwest diagonal

Let me first change the height. I'll click on the height field.
Good! The height field is now selected (showing 42 highlighted in blue). Let me type 60 to make it more elliptical.
Perfect! The height field now shows 60 in the LAYOUT section. Let me press Enter to apply this change.

Excellent! The ellipse is now taller (42×60) as shown by the dimension label "42 × 60" in the canvas. I can see the ellipse shape is now more elongated. Now I need to rotate it to 315 degrees so it aligns with the northwest diagonal direction. I need to scroll up to see the rotation field in the POSITION section.
Good! I can now see the POSITION section at the top. I can see the rotation field (∠) showing "0" in the POSITION section. Let me click on that field to enter the rotation value of 315 degrees.
Good! I can see the rotation field is now selected (the "0" is highlighted in the POSITION section, ∠ 0). Let me type 315 to rotate the petal to the northwest diagonal.
Perfect! The rotation field now shows 315 in the POSITION section (∠ 315). Let me press Enter to apply the rotation.

Excellent! The ellipse has been rotated 315 degrees and is now positioned diagonally in the northwest direction. I can see it's rotated correctly, extending up and to the left from the center. Now I need to change its color to complete the flower. This is the final eighth petal, so I need to choose a different color. Let me scroll down to see the FILL section and change the color.

Perfect! Now I can see the FILL section showing "D9D9D9" (gray color code). Let me click on the fill color square to open the color picker and change this final eighth petal to a different color. Since I've used: red, orange, magenta/pink, purple, cyan/blue, green, and teal, let me make this last one a lime/yellow-green or another distinct color.

Perfect! The color picker has opened and I can see the full color spectrum bar at the bottom with all the rainbow colors displayed. I also see the color square showing gradients from white to black with the current color in red tones. For this final eighth petal, I need to choose a color I haven't used yet. Let me select a lime/chartreuse (yellow-green) color. I'll click on the yellow-green area of the spectrum bar.

Great! The color picker is now showing yellow-green/lime tones. I can see the color square displaying yellow-green gradients from white to black. The spectrum indicator is now on the yellow-green area. Now I'll click in the top-right area of the color square to get a bright, vivid lime/chartreuse color.

Perfect! The eighth petal is now a bright lime/chartreuse color (BFEB18) and positioned at the northwest diagonal (315 degrees). I can see the flower is now complete in the canvas with all 8 colorful petals arranged radially around the yellow center circle! The color picker shows "BFEB18" in the fill section at the bottom right, and I can see a small circle indicator in the color square showing where I selected the color.

Now let me close the color picker to see the complete flower more clearly. I'll press Escape.
